concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 5 Statistical Validation (OPD) – TOST equivalence test on seed‑level accuracies
concerns.text: The plan uses the distribution of 30 seed‑level accuracy values as the sole input to a TOST equivalence test. This ignores within‑seed variability (i.e., the binomial variance of accuracy over the held‑out test items). Treating each seed’s mean accuracy as a single observation can underestimate variance, inflating power and risking false claims of equivalence.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 8 Statistical Validation (SFT) – two‑sample t‑test comparing frozen‑subspace SFT (OPD mask) to the Full‑Parameter OPD baseline
concerns.text: The SFT comparison uses the Full‑Parameter OPD baseline rather than a Full‑Parameter SFT baseline. Without a direct SFT baseline, it is unclear whether observed performance differences are due to the subspace constraint or to inherent differences between OPD and SFT objectives, confounding the test of geometric distinctness.

The loss‑plateau criterion (< 0.001 change over two epochs) is applied uniformly across all conditions, but freezing most parameters may change the effective learning dynamics (e.g., gradient magnitude). The plan does not control for this confound, making loss‑plateau timing an ambiguous indicator of “optimization compatibility.”

Power analysis is performed only for the TOST equivalence test (OPD vs frozen OPD). No power analysis is provided for the two‑sample t‑tests used in the SFT comparisons, leaving those tests potentially under‑powered.

The primary variance‑explained threshold (≥ 95 %) is treated as a design choice, yet the plan does not justify why this level is sufficient for functional subspace sufficiency. Without a principled justification, the subspace dimensionality may be arbitrarily large, threatening the “extreme sparsity” claim of the project.
